timeline.title: Prompt v1: initial meeting-analysis prompt
timeline.what_happened: AI returned generic action items such as 'Review meeting action plan' even when those tasks were not in the transcript.
timeline.how_we_knew: Manual transcript testing showed the output included filler tasks and mixed owners across multiple people.
timeline.why_it_failed: The prompt asked for a summary but did not clearly force ownership mapping or reject generic tasks.
timeline.fix: The prompt was rewritten to require real participant names, split multi-owner tasks, and block generic filler tasks unless explicitly stated in the transcript.

timeline.title: Prompt v2: improved but still weak
timeline.what_happened: Action items still sometimes had unclear owners or duplicate tasks for the same person.
timeline.how_we_knew: Regression checks and UI grouping showed duplicate entries and inconsistent owner mapping.
timeline.why_it_failed: The prompt improved, but the app still trusted AI output without post-processing validation.
timeline.fix: Added a normalization layer to remove duplicates, filter generic items, and keep only valid owner-task pairs before rendering.

timeline.title: Fallback summary path
timeline.what_happened: The app returned a summary that looked successful, but users could not tell whether it came from real AI or fallback logic.
timeline.how_we_knew: Runtime checks showed missing API keys or failed requests, yet the UI still displayed a normal-looking summary without a source label.
timeline.why_it_failed: Fallback output had the same shape as AI output, so the user could not tell the difference.
timeline.fix: Added source labels such as 'Cohere AI', 'OpenRouter AI', and 'Fallback Summary' and warning messages when no API key is available.

timeline.title: OpenRouter route
timeline.what_happened: It produced a summary, but the output quality and structure were less reliable than Cohere.
timeline.how_we_knew: The result was usable, but provider consistency was weaker for structured meeting extraction.
timeline.why_it_failed: Free/open provider variance is higher than the preferred provider route.
timeline.fix: Kept it as a backup route only and prioritized the more stable Cohere path.

timeline.title: Final prompt: ownership-aware and stable
timeline.what_happened: Outputs matched the transcript better and action items grouped correctly by person.
timeline.how_we_knew: Final transcript checks confirmed that each action item belonged to a valid participant and generic tasks were removed.
timeline.why_it_worked: The fix combined tighter prompt rules with post-processing validation, not just prompt wording alone.
timeline.fix: Combined stricter prompt constraints with owner-based normalization and display grouping before the result is shown to the user.

summary: The real issue was not only the wording of the prompt, but also the lack of strict validation after AI response generation. The stable fix was: constrain the prompt, force real owners, remove generic tasks, and clearly indicate when the system is using fallback output.
